evals.prompt: Turn this into a Slack message for the platform channel: ok so the rspack thing is done for mfe-admin-shell, refresh is like 1 second now instead of 12, i think we should roll it to the other apps but maybe not the checkout one yet? not sure. PR is github.com/acme/mfe/pull/482
evals.expected_output: One finished Slack message in the user's slack register, shorter than the ramble, keeping the numbers and the link, with the checkout question left open.
assertions: Returns one message, not alternatives or a plan
Keeps 1 second, 12, mfe-admin-shell, and the PR link verbatim
The checkout rollout stays a question or a maybe; it is not stated as a decision
No em dash or spaced hyphen
No praise, preamble, or explanation before the message

evals.prompt: Write a blog post in my voice. Facts: I rebuilt my site from scratch in one night with Claude Code, it was live before morning, the old codebase was 3 years old and I deleted all of it. That is all I want to say.
evals.expected_output: A short post in the blog register built only from the three supplied facts, with no invented motive, quote, or extra episode, halved once and checked.
assertions: Contains no reason or motive for the rebuild that the user did not state
Contains no invented numbers, names, tools, or quotes beyond one night, 3 years, and Claude Code
Follows the blog profile's exclamation, emoji, and heading conventions
No em dash or spaced hyphen
Returns the post text only

evals.prompt: Critique my draft before I send it to my manager: 'Hi Priya, I hope this finds you well. I wanted to reach out because I've been thinking about the on-call rotation and honestly I think there might potentially be some room for improvement. It's not about the workload, it's about the predictability. Let me know your thoughts when you get a chance!'
evals.expected_output: Findings ordered by cost to the reader, each naming the place, the problem, and the cost, followed by a rewritten message; no praise anywhere.
assertions: Opens with the highest-cost finding, not a compliment or a summary of what works
Contains no praise or reassurance sentence
Names the buried ask and the hedge stack as findings
Includes the rewritten message after the findings
The rewrite keeps Priya and the on-call subject and adds no invented detail

evals.prompt: Write the README for this repo. package.json: name @acme/harbor, bin harbor, description 'Ship a preview URL for every branch', repository github.com/acme/harbor, license MIT, private not set.
evals.expected_output: A CLI README from the manifest: install from the published name, a runnable quickstart, badges because it is published, no invented origin story, and the readme profile's markup if one exists.
assertions: Install line uses @acme/harbor, not the repo name
Quickstart is complete and runnable as pasted
Contains no sentence explaining why the author built it
No Contributing, Development, Tech Stack, or Workspaces section
No em dash; canonical heading names Install, Quickstart, License

evals.prompt: Write the hero headline and subhead for the Done Bear landing page. Cold Instagram traffic. It's a to-do app for people with ADHD, 2,100 paying users, syncs with Google Calendar.
evals.expected_output: One recommended headline and subhead written from the donebear profile, opening with the reader's problem, keeping 2,100 and Google Calendar, with inferred brief fields marked.
assertions: Reads the donebear profile rather than a personal one
Headline opens with the reader's problem or motivation, not the product name
2,100 and Google Calendar appear and are not replaced by generic phrases
Does not reuse the phrase 'to-do app for people with ADHD' verbatim
Returns one recommended draft with inferred fields marked

evals.prompt: Draft a Slack reply saying I agree and can review the PR tomorrow. (GHOSTWRITER_HOME points at an empty directory.)
evals.expected_output: One plain, tell-free Slack line, then a single line saying no slack profile exists yet and offering to write one from 5 to 10 pasted messages.
assertions: Returns a usable reply without stopping or refusing
Does not adopt a fictional persona, sign-off, or laugh token
Offers to write a profile from pasted samples in one line
Does not tell the user an export or training step is required

evals.prompt: Here are eight Slack messages I wrote: [eight short messages, two containing a colleague's name and a PR link]. Write my slack profile.
evals.expected_output: A slack.md under the data root in the profile shape (Register, Contexts, Message shapes, Language, Anti-patterns, Redacted excerpts, Provenance), written after one path confirmation, with names and links redacted in excerpts.
assertions: Asks once to confirm the write path before writing
Every excerpt is under 280 characters and contains no colleague name or PR link
Provenance states it is a quick profile from 8 pasted samples and not evaluable
No rule is derived from a single message
Does not point the user at an export or training step
